title: Candidate debrief: Jordan Rivera (Sr ML Engineer - Serving Runtime)
content:
Quick personal notes from ons ite loop (2/26) — raw/untidy. Shared here so Ben/Maya can pick up.

Candidate: Jordan Rivera — applied for Sr ML Engineer, Serving Runtime (focus: inference kernel optimization, latency/cost tuning)
Interviewers: Sophie Chen (me), Ben Carter (systems), Maya Singh (team fit)

High-level impression:
- Smart, pragmatic engineer. Deep systems intuition + good product sense.
- Strong at reasoning about tradeoffs (latency vs cost, batching vs tail latency).
- Less hands-on experience with attention kernel-level optimization (CUDA/TVM) than I'd expected for senior role — more infra/serving-level than low-level kernels.

Scorecard (quick, 1-5):
- Problem solving: 4/5 (clear, structured approach to open problems)
- Systems design: 4/5 (good partitioning ideas for serving pipeline)
- Coding: 4/5 (clean, explained tradeoffs; roughly 20-30 LOC exercise ok)
- Inference/LLM-specific knowledge: 3/5 (understands caching, batching, KV cache conceptually but limited on quant/kernels)
- Culture/team fit: 5/5 (collaborative, communicates clearly, excited about production constraints)

Notes by interviewer: Sophie
- Warm intro + background: has 7 yrs infra/ML infra at two startups; last role led a small infra team that shipped autoscaling and a routing layer for models. Emphasized observability and cost controls.
- Design prompt (scale chat inference to support 2M active users): walked through sharding, routing, cost tiers. Good on autoscale policies, routing by SLA. Suggested fallback model families (cheap quant variants) — practical.
- Follow-up: asked about prefix caching/kv eviction policies — proposed LRU + TTL + user-priority buckets; good clarity but no perf numbers.
- Coding exercise: implement simplified batching dispatcher — solution readable, used locks carefully, addressed head-of-line blocking. Could have mentioned non-blocking ring buffer approach but approach acceptable.

Notes by Ben (systems):
- Strong on observability and debugging. Gave specific examples of tracing injected into RPC stack.
- Less hands-on with low-level GPU perf work (no TVM/CUTLASS examples), but has experience choosing prebuilt ops and tuning batch sizes.

Notes by Maya (team fit):
- Very collaborative, asked good onboarding questions. Seems motivated by impact rather than prestige.
- Good mentorship examples, has coached junior engs on performance reviews and runbook playbooks.

Concerns / open questions:
- Kernel-level optimization experience (CUDA/assembly/TVM) is limited; depends on whether PM expects senior to do low-level tuning or focus on orchestration/serving.
- No published perf microbenchmarks from prior roles; asked for examples in follow-up email (resume link points to blog post about platform but not deep kernel work).
- Availability timeline: said flexible but needs 4 weeks after offer. Compensation expectations aligned with bar.

Recommendation (my take):
- Proceed to take-home or final loop if the role is focused on serving/platform and orchestration (routing, autoscale, caching). Jordan will be strong contributor here.
- If role requires deep GPU/kernel engineering (low-level CUDA/ops), we should either: 1) set expectation and test in take-home OR 2) prefer candidates with explicit kernel experience.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben/Maya to weigh in on kernel vs platform split (reply in thread).
- If team agrees platform-focused hire: invite to take-home (systems-focused) + 60m with PM to discuss roadmap.
- Ask Jordan for links/examples of perf work (promised to share a small internal benchmark doc) — follow up: Maya to ping recruiting to request artifacts.

Misc/links I dropped during convo:
- Confluence: hiring rubric for Sr ML Eng (link above)
- GitHub: suggested reading for batching strategies (internal repo references)
notes_summary: Candidate recommended for platform-focused senior role; limited low-level kernel/CUDA exposure; strong systems design, observability, and team fit. Suggest take-home if role is orchestration/serving-first.
